name: revolver

motions.note: cock: -55 deg about the node's +X axis (glTF) swings the spur rearward (top goes back) - spur ends ~10 mm behind the frame; pivot = hammer pin.
pull: +20 deg about +X (glTF) swings the finger blade rearward (double action); pivot = trigger pin.

swing-out: rotate the crane (carries `cylinder`, ejector rod, eject/mag_well sockets) by -70 deg about the node's +Z axis (glTF forward, right-hand rule) -> the cylinder swings out to the LEFT (+X) and slightly up. Pivot = crane hinge pin (x=104, left y=+16, z=33 mm in gun mm).
index: spins about its own axis (local +Z glTF); 60 deg per chamber (either direction; real Colts turn clockwise seen from the rear). Origin = cylinder centre. It is a CHILD of `crane`.

remarks: Reload: swing the crane out (-70 deg), punch cases out rearward via `eject` (crane child), drop fresh rounds into the chambers at `mag_well` (cylinder centre), swing back. Six brass .357 rounds are modelled in the chambers.
Hands: right hand on the wood grip at grip_R (index on the trigger); support hand cups the left grip panel at grip_L. Hammer spur is ~ 10 mm from the web of the hand when cocked.

Socket orientations: `eject` +X points REARWARD (out of the cylinder rear when the crane is open), it and `mag_well` are children of `crane` so they follow the swing. `muzzle`/`grip_R`/`sight` are static.
Ejector rod is inside `cylinder` and hides in the full underlug bore when closed. `sight` sits 60 mm behind the frame at the sight-line height (over the rear notch).
